statement: For a Noetherian Q-domain R, every rational function F over Frac(R) taking R-values at infinitely many integers has a presentation A/B with A,B in R[T] and B(n0)=1 at one integer. Over a local R, a finite torsion-free module version has a denominator nonzero modulo the maximal ideal.

depends_on: Nagata (1996), printed p. 998, definition and Lemmas 1.1–1.2
Finite integral extension generated by finitely many integral coefficients
notes: No finite-normalization hypothesis. The proof starts with an infinite good integer set and removes only finitely many integers. The module assertion explicitly requires locality. Nagata 1955 is cited by the checked 1996 source but was not independently opened; no priority claim is made.

statement: Every fibrewise quasi-unipotent section of a separated finitely presented group scheme over a Noetherian Q-scheme has a positive power on a global Ga. The base may be reducible or nonreduced, and the group need not be affine, flat or smooth. The parameter through a fixed value at 1 is unique.
where_proved: sections/D_surface.tex, D.18: primary local rings, saturated nilpotent filtration, integer translations, closed patching and globalization
depends_on: D.11 and its finite Artinian iteration
Finite primary decomposition in a Noetherian ring
notes: The primary filtration is I_j=A∩rad(B)^j, not the generally nonsaturated powers of rad(A). The modules I_j/I_{j+1} are finite torsion-free over A/rad(A). Closed patching uses uniqueness on the full scheme-theoretic overlap with the previously patched union. All integer sections in the affine chart form a cofinite set; infinitely many suffice for D.17.

statement: For an arbitrary local ring A and a separated finitely presented group G/A, an additive parameter for a positive power of a fibrewise quasi-unipotent section over A[1/n] extends, after another positive power, over A. The integer n may be a zerodivisor; A need not be Noetherian.
where_proved: sections/D_surface.tex, D.19: coordinate lift, finite relation errors, group-law and commutation equalizers, and torsion correction
depends_on: D.13 constructible compactness and finite nilpotent ideal argument
notes: The initial scheme map has value e at 0 exactly. Every relation, group-law and commutation error has zero constant coefficient and finitely many n-power-torsion coefficients, killed by an additional dilation. The correction δ commutes with the parameter value, is fibrewise finite order and equals 1 after inverting n. Its finitely generated equalizer ideal is both nilpotent and n-power torsion. Every finiteness claim comes from finite presentation, so Noetherianity is unnecessary.

statement: Every fibrewise quasi-unipotent section of a separated finitely presented group scheme over an arbitrary Noetherian base has a positive power on a global Ga, without reducedness, irreducibility, regularity or flatness assumptions.

statement: Every fibrewise quasi-unipotent section of a separated finitely presented group scheme over any quasi-compact quasi-separated base has a positive power on a global Ga. No Noetherian, affine, smooth or flat hypothesis is needed.
where_proved: sections/D_surface.tex, D.21: constructible witness images, compactness, Noetherian approximation, arbitrary-ring integer localization and descent
notes: No representability of Hom_gp(Ga,G) is assumed. Each field witness spreads to a finite-type witness scheme; its constructible image remains in the quasi-unipotence locus by characteristic-zero uniqueness and fpqc descent. Compactness gives finitely many such images covering Spec R; vanishing of the constructible complement descends via finitely many explicit ring identities. D.14 still refutes the original hypothesis of quasi-compactness alone. The group in this theorem is finitely presented, not merely locally finitely presented.

statement: Every continuous homomorphism from a profinite group M to the finite-adèle points of an affine finite-type Q-group H admits a smooth affine finite-type Z-model containing its image in H(Ẑ), with any specified rational character extending over Z. Subgroups whose image is diagonal rational have integral image. No connectedness of H is required.
